claims.claim: Reviewers describe the open world as empty and missions as repetitive and checklist-driven.

citations.review_text:
This game genuinely made my PC fans blow out the most horrendous-smelling air.

Wildlands feels like Ubisoft took a massive map, filled it with copy-pasted missions, collectibles, outposts, and pointless objectives, and called it a game. After a while, it becomes an endless cycle of driving somewhere, killing everyone, grabbing an objective, and doing the exact same thing again.

And I'm not the only one who noticed. Reviewers have criticized the repetitive missions, empty open world, bugs, awkward AI, and overall lack of variety. PCWorld described the world as feeling empty despite its enormous size, while Ars Technica criticized the repetitive structure and technical issues. PC Gamer also pointed out how quickly the mission templates become repetitive.

The massive open world sounds impressive until you realize most of it is just empty space between nearly identical missions. Even GameSpot noted that the game's motivation and rewards can start wearing thin despite the huge map.

The bugs, awkward AI, mediocre driving, repetitive objectives, and Ubisoft-style bloat make this feel less like a tactical Ghost Recon game and more like a giant checklist simulator.

claims.claim: Players on newer Intel processors with E-cores or hyperthreading are unable to launch the game without disabling those CPU features in their BIOS.

citations.review_text:
This game is being sold, and updated with new DLC, while containing outdated EAC and other issues that prevent the game from running on hardware that uses Hyperthreading or more modern core infrastructure. The discussion forums are full of people having this issue. People who never had the issue before, like myself, cannot launch into the game anymore. The game used to work fine until recent updates and a DLC injection. Ubisoft has been informed of this and has confirmed with people on support tickets that they are aware of the issue but do not plan to patch it out. 

Apparently that's not stopping them from rebranding into a marked up "Definitive Edition" that costs you $100.

Might be time to push for a Class Action Lawsuit that holds them accountable for defrauding consumers, as several of their other games have this same issue.

Don't buy this until it's patched at least. Or just don't buy it.

THE GOOD:

- 25th anniversary update added a new mission and re-added the fan favourite predator mission.
- you get all gun attachements immediately which is nice
- they added options similar to breakpoints "ghost experience", HUD settings and 


THE BAD:

- you can no longer earn the blue premium store credits to buy any of the remaining locked premium stuff because Daily/Weekly challenges have been entirely removed. "You can earn most of the content in the game through play." doesnt apply anymore because of how much previously unlockable through game preogression has been paywalled

- all three types of loot crates have been removed. the menu for them is still there but YOU CANT CLAIM ANY CRATES YOU ALREADY OWN, EVEN THE ONE YOU GET FOR FREE WHICH IS INSANELY FUNNY

- basically they removed the entire endgame gameplay loop and put the rewards you could previously earn from gameplay into the cash shop instead.

- if you want the whole game you have to buy the newly added "definitive edition upgrade" time to pay up!


THE TECHNICAL BAD:
- the game is packed with a old version of EasyAntiCheat which made my system very instable. Last time i had this issue was with Elden Rings version of EAC. This results into crashes to desktop up to OS freezing up completely.

- YOU CANNOT RUN THE GAME if your CPU has more than 8 cores, efficiency cores/hyperthreading. You need to disable efficiency cores or disable hyperthreading in your BIOS/UEFI to make the game boot up!

- loading in the game or after getting killed takes up to five minutes. I have had the game on a freshly bought SSD.

if you want to play the game normally you have to sail the seven seas :)
back to metal gear solid v- the phantom pain and ghost recon: breakpoint i go!
Dont buy this game if you have intel core ultra processors because the devs do not want to fix the cpu issue and infinite loading screen.

A 10 GB update and they still haven't fixed the issue where you can't launch the game if you use an Intel 12th+ generation CPU (CPUs with ECores fail to launch the game). If you have an older Intel CPU or an AMD CPU, you should have a good time. 

With that being said it is a great game. 

However, since after several years with no updates and then release one recently and they still don't patch a known issue. Thumbs down.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the open world map is extremely large and packed with repetitive missions, collectibles, and activities.

citations.review_text:
[h1]“A qué estás esperando? Vamos a partirles la madre con todo. Disparen!”[/h1]

~27 hours on Steam, ~50 hours total across PS4, Xbox Series S, and PC. Finished the main campaign + true ending, ignored almost all side content.

[b]7.5/10 — Buy it only on sale. Just the base game not definitive edition.[/b]

[h2]The Good[/h2]

[b]+ The gameplay[/b]
Stealth + shooting + drone scouting + squad commands make for a genuinely fun tactical loop. Scan the area, mark everyone, Sync Shot a few guys, sneak in, then starts shooting when things gone south.

[b]+ Tactical without being too hardcore[/b]
It gives you enough tools to feel clever without turning into a military simulator.

[b]+ The world[/b]
Huge, beautiful, and surprisingly diverse. Different regions actually feel different, and the graphics still hold up pretty well for a 2017 game.

[b]+ The villains[/b]
Each antagonist has their own story and personality, and their introduction videos are genuinely interesting. They do a good job giving some variety to an otherwise repetitive mission structure.

[h2]The Bad[/h2]

[b]- Peak Ubisoft bloat[/b]
The map is [b]way too damn big[/b]. Collectibles, supplies, weapons, attachments, activities, icons everywhere. I ignored almost all of it and rushed the main campaign.

[b]- Repetitive as hell[/b]
Around the 10-hour mark, you've pretty much seen the formula. Most missions are the same basic idea wearing a different shirt. Escort and tailing missions can go straight into the bin.

[b]- The writing[/b]
[b]Cringe.[/b] Cliché dialogue, weak banter, and repeated lines despite only doing the main campaign.

[strike]Come Mierda Culeros.[/strike]

[b]Pac Katari[/b] deserved way more presence instead of mostly existing through radio calls. 
[b]Bowman and Sueno[/b] are the only on that got the voice acting well. Everyone else is just okay.

[b]- The AI[/b]
Great at Sync Shot. Absolutely questionable at anything resembling actual tactics. Give them an order and they'll occasionally for…
pretty good, but each mission is almost exactly the same

Even though this game might be a bit repetitive. It is still a very good time. Especially with friends.
Its a great loop. Not as bloated as AC Valhalla, or Odyssey. I'd still never buy a Ubisoft game at full price though.
Intel users be warned, this game requires optimization to play on newer hardware. This game wasn't made with hyperthreading in mind.

Ghost Recon Wildlands has been out for a few years now, and it still holds up remarkably well in 2026 .

The Bolivia map is one of the most underrated open worlds in the genre . 
It's not just big for the sake of being big: you go from dazzling salt flats to dense jungles to snowy Andean peaks, and each region has its own visual and tactical identity . 
It genuinely changes how you approach missions .

The freedom of approach is real: pure stealth, frontal assault, remote sabotage... the game never really forces your hand .

The enemy AI has clearly shown its age detection is sometimes inconsistent, and once you're spotted, the game often shifts into a standard firefight rather than a tense infiltration . 
The story is also fairly forgettable, more of a pretext to string objectives together than a memorable narrative . 
And solo, without coop, it clearly loses intensity .

One small regret too: the Narco Road and Fallen Ghosts expansions, while enjoyable, are completely separate from the main campaign and don't share the same save file . 
You can't bring your character or your progressed gear from the base game into them, which breaks the continuity a bit and makes it feel like two isolated bubbles rather than proper additional content integrated into the adventure .

Wildlands isn't perfect, but it's a generous tactical sandbox, especially in coop, and remains a solid reference point for anyone looking for a no nonsense military open world game . 
Solo or with 3 friends and some time on your hands, go for it .

I paid for Tom Clancy’s Ghost Recon Wildlands on Steam, but apparently purchasing the game doesn’t mean I actually get to play it.

I changed phone numbers and no longer have access to the phone number connected to Ubisoft’s two-step authentication. Because of that, I cannot log into my Ubisoft account or even get through the launcher to play the game I purchased.

I tried creating a new Ubisoft account thinking I could at least start fresh. Nope. The game refuses to launch because my Steam purchase is linked to my old Ubisoft account, not the new one.

So now I’m stuck in this ridiculous situation: I purchased the game on Steam, the game is installed through Steam, but I cannot play it because I lost access to a phone number connected to a completely separate Ubisoft account.

The game itself might be good, but none of that matters when the launcher/account system prevents a paying customer from accessing their purchase.

Requiring a separate launcher, Ubisoft account, account linking, AND two-step authentication just to access a game purchased through Steam is incredibly frustrating.

Deeply unsatisfied. If you're considering buying Wildlands on Steam, be aware that your ability to access the game can still depend on your Ubisoft account and launcher.

I'm writing this review while I wait for GR: Wildlands to load.

On newer hardware, specifically, it seems, Raptor Lake CPU's, the game takes between 15-20 minutes to boot. This is unacceptable considering they recently "updated" the game.
Furthermore, the previous method of end-game grinding has been rendered inert with the removal of the lootboxes - now the only way to unlock certain weapons and cosmetics is to purchase them. Typical Ubisoft L.

So, my 251 hours? Those were obtained back when the game worked.

This has been a problem for years that is well documented, yet there isn't a patch for it. This mostly seems to impact Intel CPUs, so buyer-beware here; You can work around it by disabling e-cores in the BIOS supposedly, but I do more than play Wildlands on this machine, so I'm not doing that. Alternatively, some folks only have to wait 10-15 minutes for the game to load if they are lucky, so if you have that time to waste? Go right ahead.

It's a great game, but right now Ubisoft isn't really offering even basic support for it anymore (and yes, support tickets had been created years ago when the issue came about). It's all but abandoned except for the cash grab.

Wildlands has been one of my favourite games for years, and it's been great to see it be given some much needed love for the 25th Anniversary. The free update, QOL features, Last Rites mission, re-licensing the Predator mission, and anniversary gifts are awesome- and I can fully understand a few bugs coming along with poking about a nearly decade old game.

But Ubisoft's keen-as-ever buisness acumen on this is borderline insane.

Good news is a bunch of the premium store stuff has been rebundled at lower costs, or made free entirely.

Bad news is you can no longer earn the blue premium store credits to buy any of it because Daily/Weekly challenges have seemingly been entirely removed, as have all three types of loot crates.

Meaning no more blue credits from duplicate drops. This also means any prestige credits you can still earn (through say Tier 1 mode) can go towards little to nothing (boosters, supply points, skill points). Even if I bought what I could it looks like I'll permanantly be stuck with 75 of them because nothing in the store deals in denominations of less than a hundred. In addition it looks like any previously crate related item that remains locked is now fully paywalled in the store and can now only be bought via Microtransaction purchased credits. Taking previously earnable content in a beloved game and paywalling after this long it is dastardly work Ubisoft.

This also kills the classic promise of "You can earn most of the content in the game through play." as the one way to very slowly earn that premium content as I've been doing by coming back to GR Wildlands near daily for months on end in order to buy one or two of the weapon packs that interested me- is now removed from the game.

This is also the one thing that had kept me coming back regularly to play. The daily challenges were easily replayable and mostly entertaining remixes on completed missions with unique constraints- and community goals were endearing to see chipped away. I really ho…
Ubislop greedily took out content you could get playing the game and put it behind real money transactions. I'm never buying anything from this company again

A great open world, full player agency tactical simulator for assassinating drug lords and dismantling a sprawling cartel network.

World building is top notch and weaponry and vehicle variety is amazing.

Enemy AI becomes annoying infinite spawning aimbots in advanced tier one mode and stealth becomes the only viable playstyle.

Predator boss fight is absolute a$$.

To "celebrate" 25th year Tom Clancy anniversary, Ubi$hit removed all loot crates and earned game currency and locked every in-game item behind paywalls... Removing the only replay value incentive to collect all the guns.

Such a d!ck move.

Update: their August 14, 2026 patch causes the game to crash repeatedly with IRQ fault hard reboot or soft locks. Don't bother buying / playing this anymore.

They updated the game... Kinda. 
They paywalled things you used to be able to earn. lol
Classic Ubisoft move

citations.review_text: GREEDDDDY. Changing a game I already bought with paywalls... Cool

Stuck on the splash? Disable hyper-threading. Crashing while/after the attachments screen? Uninstall.

All DLC including La Llorna are separate from the campaign, so any progress made in the campaign will not carry over to any DLC and vice versa.

Before this update, weapons, attachments and clothing were unlockable by just playing the game. 3/4 of all weapons, attachments and clothing are now locked behind a paywall. This is to make up in lost revenue from their recent failures and to prolong their survival during bankruptcy. Classic ubisoft.

It would be cool if Wildlands had the same movement as Breakpoint. The only thing I hate right now is that they removed the daily challenges, which sucks because it means you’ll have to buy everything.
